title: fm owns crew lifetimes with visible Herdr dispatch; alternative detached hosts remain deferred
acceptance: Why: preserve scripted zero-model supervision under the approved 2026-10-01 plan. The older optional-host/headless-default proposal is superseded by T-151 lifelines, T-162 visible Herdr/cmuxOnly policy and design section 15.7. Commit this task spec; it remains a basic-pilot prerequisite, not an advanced autopilot dependency.

Start and supervise each worker/reviewer through bin/lib/fm_lifeline.py or bin/lib/fm-lifeline.sh with a named durable fm session/service owner. Preserve sandbox, timeouts, lost-crew reporting, bounded retries, stdout/stderr, stop and descendant reaping. No setsid, detached process bypass, PID polling or beacon liveness. Run identity and pushed completion bind final output and cleanup to that owner.

Standard stock dispatch retains a visible owned Herdr window with labelled live output and board focus. Keep fm_refuse_herdr_bypass and cmuxOnly protections. A view is not the owner: view closure or crash must be reported and repaired through the supported path without abandoning ownership; the owned run ends with its named owner. Dispatcher exit must not prematurely end a successfully handed-off run; capture the durable handoff. T-051 supplies the external integration without waiting for T-141.

Optional host:none, tmux and full detached cmux lifecycle are historical proposals, explicitly deferred; this task does not enable a headless-default or a raw vendor pane path. Preserve accepted cmuxOnly routing and truthful refusal where no supported visible host can launch.

Tests cover stock dispatch, labelled live Herdr view and board focus, dispatcher-to-durable-owner handoff, view loss, owner exit/reaping, duplicate launch, final output and cleanup/retention. Dynamic board summaries carry en and zh-TW. Required GitHub checks and six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7 plus a captured live pilot establish acceptance; workers author feature-owned fail-first tests but run no suites. Stubs match real host/transport behavior.
